audience.programmeDescription: German Language and Culture at Leiden combines intensive German-language study with literature, linguistics and cultural history. Students interpret texts and media, investigate language change and variation, and study identity and memory across German-speaking societies. A period at a German-speaking university and an individual research thesis connect these strands. Compulsory first-year mentoring supports academic study skills.
audience.comparisonExplanation: A complete UCR comparison awaits confirmation of one required 5-EC part of the external curriculum. The supported components below provide a partial view. This uncertainty does not establish that UCR offers no suitable study possibilities.

curriculum.limitation: The supported components total 175 EC. One required 5-EC component remains unclear, so this is an incomplete curriculum rather than a certified 180-EC degree plan. Mentoring and the thesis seminar carry no additional credits.

componentNotes.y1-german-1: Intensive practice in German reading, listening, speaking and writing, including grammar, vocabulary and pronunciation. This foundation supports later language and subject study.
componentNotes.y1-medieval-literature: Literature and cultural history from the early Middle Ages through the Baroque. The course is counted once in the supported total.
componentNotes.y2-abroad: 25 EC of compulsory study at a German-speaking university. Courses must suit the programme and receive prior approval through a Learning Agreement. Entry requires the first-year programme, advanced German and language history.
componentNotes.y3-literature-americas: The selected 10-EC literature seminar examines European–American encounters in German-language writing. Its substantial paper precedes the literature thesis.
componentNotes.y3-language-variation: The selected 10-EC linguistics seminar studies variation in contemporary German and the social evaluation of language varieties. Linguistic, literary and cultural focus areas are academic choices, rather than named formal degree routes.
componentNotes.y3-thesis: A 10-EC individual research thesis in literary studies, following substantial written work in that discipline. The compulsory thesis seminar is included without separate credit.
componentNotes.y3-electives: 30 EC of genuine elective space, for options such as a minor, an approved course package or an internship. Approval and level rules apply; the overlapping German language, culture and history minor is excluded.
